title: Finding the core vs flexible microbiome
author: Bonnie Hurwitz
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.d2y8fv

steps.title: Locate fasta files
steps.instruction: Navigate to /iplant/home/shared/imicrobe/class/obese_lean and note the four fasta files: SRR029687.fasta (lean T1), SRR029692.fasta (lean T2), SRR029686.fasta (obese T19), SRR029688.fasta (obese T20).

steps.title: Run uproc on each fasta
steps.instruction: In iPlant, click Apps → experimental → imicrobe → uproc, open Required Args, use Browse to select each fasta file (e.g., /iplant/home/shared/imicrobe/class/obese_lean/SRR029687.fasta) under "Sequence file", and run uproc with default parameters. Repeat for all four fasta files.

steps.title: Download dataset via iRODS
steps.instruction: Log into the HPC, load the iRODS module with `module load irods`, change to the shared directory using `icd /iplant/home/shared/imicrobe/class`, and download the entire obese_lean directory recursively with `iget -r obese_lean`.

steps.title: Initialize iRODS configuration
steps.instruction: If this is your first iRODS use, run `iinit` and provide the following settings: host = data.iplantcollaborative.org; port = 1247; zone = iplant; user = your iPlant username; login = your iPlant login.

steps.title: Copy and rename uproc outputs
steps.instruction: Create a local folder for the results and rename each uproc output:

substeps.instruction: For each analysis, change to its iPlant analysis directory, e.g., `icd /iplant/home/your_user/analyses/uproc_SRR029687-your-analysis`
Rename it to the sample name with `.uproc` extension, e.g., `mv uproc-out SRR029687.uproc`
Repeat the three commands for SRR029692, SRR029686, and SRR029688

steps.title: Identify core KEGG IDs
steps.instruction: Write a Perl script named `get_core.pl` that parses the four .uproc files (T1, T2, T19, T20) and outputs KEGG IDs that appear in all four files with at least 50 read matches. The script should produce a list of core KEGG IDs.

steps.title: Identify variable KEGG IDs
steps.instruction: Write a Perl script named `get_variable.pl` that parses the same .uproc files and outputs KEGG IDs that appear in 1–3 of the files (but not all four) with at least 50 read matches. The script should produce a list of variable KEGG IDs.

steps.title: Combine core and variable scripts
steps.instruction: Merge the functionality of `get_core.pl` and `get_variable.pl` into a single script called `get_core_and_variable.pl` that outputs both the core and variable KEGG ID lists.

steps.title: Submit scripts and results
steps.instruction: Upload the Perl scripts and their output files to the GitHub repository under the folder abe487/obese_lean.
